title: Inward path close
hook: the stations, the diseases, the manners, the virtues: one heart, rusted and polished

segments.voice: Yesterday, ihsan, and your line: excellence in everything. Did one ordinary task get its last corner finished? Today the inward path closes, and we look at the whole road at once. Day one thousand three hundred seventeen.

A copper pot left in a damp shed goes dull, then green. Nobody did anything to it. It just sat, and the air did the rest. Bring it inside, rub it with a cloth, and the shine comes back, a patch at a time. The Qur'an uses that picture for the heart. In surah al-Mutaffifin, in Pickthall's translation: "Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts." Rust can gather. And what gathers can be wiped. Today: the whole inward path, as one long polishing.
screen: `A COPPER POT GOES DULL.` → `RUST UPON THEIR HEARTS.` → `WHAT GATHERS CAN BE WIPED.`

segments.voice: Start where this block started its heart days: the lump of flesh. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase: in the body is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart. Then Jami' at-Tirmidhi explains the rust. In paraphrase: when a servant sins, a black spot is marked on his heart. If he leaves it, seeks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished. If he returns to it, the spot spreads. And that, the hadith says, is the rust Allah mentions. Now the whole road, read through that picture. First, the stations, among them repentance, watchfulness, patience, gratitude, reliance, love, sincerity. They're the direction, the way the heart is meant to face. Second, the diseases: arrogance, envy, showing off, anger, greed, backbiting, lying, heedlessness, despair. That's the rust itself, named one by one, so it can be seen. Third, the manners, the adab: of speech, of eating, of guests, of travel, of sleep, of learning, of the road and the market, with parents, neighbors, children, animals and the earth. That's the daily cloth, small wipes, done every day. Fourth, the virtues: humility, generosity, modesty, truthfulness, pardon, gentleness, justice, ties of kin, loving for others, contentment, and ihsan over all of them. That's the shine coming back. Not four subjects. One heart, facing the right way, seeing its rust, wiped daily, and starting to shine.
screen: `THE STATIONS: WHICH WAY TO FACE.` · `THE DISEASES: THE RUST, NAMED.` · `THE MANNERS: THE DAILY CLOTH.` · `THE VIRTUES: THE SHINE RETURNS.`

segments.voice: The practice: name the trait you most want. Settle, and breathe. Let the road pass by slowly: patience, gratitude, sincerity; gentleness, justice, contentment; the manners of the table and the road. Don't choose quickly. Wait for the one that lands, the one you'd most like to be true of you a year from now. Name it, quietly, once. Then picture one small wipe of the cloth toward it today. If you pray, you can ask Allah for that trait by its name. The bell holds the time.
Inward path close. The stations, the diseases, the manners and the virtues, gathered into one picture: a heart that rusts, and can be polished. Today's word.

Your line: polish the heart. Today, practice the trait you named once, on purpose, and notice the patch that shines. Tomorrow a new block begins, the life cycle, with the call in the ear. Day one thousand three hundred seventeen.
